hints.title: Condition on the first draw
hints.body: There are n balls of each of three colours. Whichever colour appears first, the numbers of same-colour and different-colour balls remaining have the same form.
hints.recap: Equal initial colour counts let you analyse one first-colour case.
hints.pitfall: The first ball is not replaced.
hints.pause: How many balls remain after the first draw?

recall.reminder: Equal initial colour counts let you analyse one first-colour case.

solution:
Suppose the first ball is red. Of the 3n−1 balls left, n−1 are red and 2n are yellow or blue. The probability of a different colour on the second draw is therefore 2n/(3n−1).

The same calculation holds when the first ball is yellow or blue, because the initial colour counts are equal. Thus the unconditional probability has the same value.

Answer C. The complement check is 1−(n−1)/(3n−1)=2n/(3n−1).
